pages.text: Winding is $(l)exact-tier$(): cobblestone only winds into a T1 spool, netherite only into a T6. Feed eight winders from one chest and you normally need a hand-built sort line per tier.$(br2)The $(item)Filament Tier Item Sorter$() does it for you. Drop items into its $(l)9-slot pool$() and each one is delivered to the winder holding a spool of $(l)that item's tier$().

pages.title: Finding Winders
pages.text: The sorter looks at all $(l)six of its faces$(). A winder touching it is found directly, no cable needed at all.$(br2)To reach more than six, run $(item)MC3D Cable$(): the sorter reads every winder across the connected network. The cable only $(l)tells it where they are$(): items are never stored in or carried through a cable, they go straight from the pool into the winder.

pages.title: What It Refuses
pages.text: Two things can never be wound:$(br)$(li)items with $(l)no Filament Unit value$()$(li)items on the $(l)winder blacklist$() (sticks and friends)$(br)A winder would accept them and then jam forever, so the sorter never hands them to one.$(br2)What happens to them instead is up to you.

pages.title: Catching Rejects
pages.text: Put a $(item)chest$() against $(l)any face$() of the sorter and un-windable items are pushed into it instead of refused, so you can aim a completely unsorted stream at the sorter.$(br2)Any container works: chest, barrel, hopper, or another mod's pipe. Attach several and it fills them in turn, $(l)splitting a stack$() if the first runs out of room, so there's $(l)nothing to configure$().$(br2)MC3DPrint machines are $(l)never$() used as the target, so an adjacent winder won't get handed junk.

pages.title: When It Fills
pages.text: Once the chest is full the sorter goes back to refusing. Nothing is voided and nothing drops on the floor: your hoppers just back up, the same signal as a full pool.$(br2)With $(l)no container attached$() nothing changes from before: un-windable items are turned away at the door, including shift-clicks by hand.$(br2)Don't wire one pipe to both feed the sorter and drain the reject chest, or the junk will loop between them. Nothing is lost, but it $(l)won't stop on its own$() while something keeps emptying that chest.$(br2)If a pooled item stops being windable later, it leaves the same way, as long as routing is on and a target has room.$(br2)Reject routing is $(l)on by default$(). $(l)rejectRouting$() in the config turns off only that, never the sorter.

pages.title: What It Holds
pages.text: Everything else is kept and retried: no winder of that tier yet, the winder's input slot is busy, or its spool has no room.$(br2)Items are $(l)never voided$(). When the pool fills up, your hoppers back up. That's the signal. The GUI shows a per-tier readout ($(l)how many are waiting$() and $(l)how many winders$() it can see) so you know which tier is stuck.$(br2)The pool is a $(l)one-way funnel$(): a hopper can feed it, but nothing can pull items back out.

pages.title: Sharing the Load
pages.text: Two winders on the same tier both get fed. The sorter alternates between them $(l)round-robin$(), and skips any that would stall: a full spool or a busy input slot never wastes a turn, the item just goes to the next one.$(br2)It moves up to $(l)4 items per tick$() by default (configurable 1-64), and costs $(l)no RF at all$(): it runs completely unpowered.
The Filament Tier Item Sorter. One chest in, every tier sorted out.
